title: Bill to teach students Critical Media and Info Literacy aims to counter fake news
summary: A bill requiring a Critical Media and Information Literacy subject across all levels of the Philippine educational system has been filed in the House of Representatives.

blocks.text: A bill requiring a Critical Media and Information Literacy subject across all levels of the Philippine educational system has been filed in the House of Representatives.
House Deputy Minority Leader Antonio Tinio of ACT Teachers party-list and Representatives Sarah Elago of Gabriela and Renee Co of Kabataan made the proposal under House Bill 12061.

The authors said that the Critical Media and Information Literacy subject would cover topics beyond basic technical or analytical skills and critical media literacy, and involves an ideological critique of media representations, an analysis of power dynamics underpinning information control, and the activeproduction of alternative media.

The authors said the measure is urgent given that information is now easily digested through posts, tweets, and videos seen in various social media platforms, a situation that has led to the democratization of information production and dissemination—but also one that can be controlled by powerful political and economic actors to systematically manufacture public consent and distort reality at the same time.

“There is a prevalence of Al-generated content, in which individuals can freely alter data, structure its legitimacy, imitating information produced by authorized media institutions. Without thorough assessment and fact-checking, it is no longer unacceptable to say that the public is exposed to a wide variety of news, the truthfulness of which ranging from most reliable to most questionable,” the bill read.

The lawmakers said the advent of sophisticated artificial intelligence (AI) tools has also exponentially increased the scale and believability of fabricated content, from deepfake videos to Al-generated news articles, creating an environment where distinguishing fact from malicious fiction requires advanced analytical skills.

“This bill seeks to transform Filipino students from passive recipients of information into empowered, critical citizens capable of defending democratic discourse from manipulation and fostering a culture of truth-seeking and civic engagement,” the bill added.
Co, for her part, said the subject will train students to go beyond memorization and sharpen comprehension.
"Dapat sanayin ang bawat estudyante na kumwestiyon, mag-imbestiga, at sumalungat sa kasinungalingan. Huwag tayo basta na lang mag-scroll at maniwala sa kung ano ang nakikita sa screen," Co said.
(We should train our students to ask questions, investigate and fight lies. We must learn not to simply scroll and believe everything we see online.)
"Pag mulat at kritikal ang kabataan, hindi sila basta-basta mabubudol ng mga fake news peddlers. Sila mismo ang magiging bantay ng katotohanan at demokrasya," she added.
(If the students are aware and critical, they won't easily fall to fake news peddlers. Instead, they will be the guardrails of truth and democracy.)
